# Erweiterte karten-navigation (2026-02-05 15:11Z)

_**User**_

Ich habe bereits in einer gänzlich anderen App einen Navigations-UseCase umgesetzt. 

Wenn ein User in den Reverse-Navigations-Modus schaltet und per Doppel-Tap die Karte gänzlich auf Navigation schaltet möchte ich dass bestimmte Änderungen an MapMarker-Darstellung, Karten-Animation, Darstellung der Blickrichtung und Kamera vorgenommen werden.

Diese Änderungen habe ich im Folgenden als Plan dokumentiert und möchte dass Du daraus einen neuen Plan erstellst um DIESE Applikation und den dortigen Double-Tap Navigationsmodus anzupassen.

Hier die Spezifikation aus der anderen App:

# Plan: Map-Navigation-Verhalten übertragen

## Zielbild der Features (Was genau kopiert werden soll)

- **User-Location-Annotation mit Blickrichtung**: Custom-Annotation, die eine Richtungspfeil-Form zeichnet und die Pfeilrotation um die aktuelle Kartenrotation korrigiert.
- **Blickrichtungs-Logik**: Heading wird aus Course/Compass gemischt, geglättet und als `userHeading` + `isHeadingValid` veröffentlicht.
- **Kartenrotation + Follow-Camera**: In Navigation (inkl. Urgent) wird die Karte um die Blickrichtung gedreht; ansonsten bleibt North-up. Kamera-Updates sind weich animiert.
- **Navigation Overlay**: `NavigationOverlayKit` zeigt Instruktionen + Distanz; Fortschritt wird kontinuierlich aktualisiert.
- **Urgent-Navigation**: Route wird berechnet/gefittet, initiale Zoom-Sequenz startet, anschließend kontinuierliche Follow-Updates inkl. Rotation.

## Kernmechanik als umsetzbare Blaupause

### 1) User-Location-Annotation inkl. korrekter Pfeilrotation

- In der SwiftUI `Map` wird **eine eigene Annotation** verwendet (nicht das Standard-User-Pin).
- Pfeil-Rotation berücksichtigt Map-Rotation: `heading - mapHeading`.
- Die Karte liefert `mapHeading` via `onMapCameraChange` (siehe Schritt 3).

#### Gestaltung des MapMarkers (Circle-Layer + Heading-Arrow)

- **Layer-Aufbau (von hinten nach vorn)**:
  - Außenring: `Circle().fill(Color.accentColor.opacity(0.16)).frame(width: 36, height: 36)`
  - Kontur: `Circle().stroke(Color.accentColor.opacity(0.5), lineWidth: 2).frame(width: 28, height: 28)`
  - Innerer Kern: `Circle().fill(Color.white.opacity(0.8)).frame(width: 22, height: 22)`
    - Drop-Shadow: `.shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.15), radius: 3, x: 0, y: 2)`
  - Heading-Pfeil: `HeadingArrowShape()` in `accentColor`, nur sichtbar wenn `isHeadingValid`
  - Punktkern: `Circle().fill(Color.accentColor).frame(width: 10, height: 10)`
- **Pfeil-Form (HeadingArrowShape)**:
  - Dreieck mit Spitze oben (negative Y): `tipY = -11`, `baseY = 2`, `halfBase = 4.5`
  - Punkte: `(0, tipY)`, `(halfBase, baseY)`, `(-halfBase, baseY)`; dann `closeSubpath`
  - Anschließend zur Mitte des `rect` verschoben (`translationX: rect.midX, y: rect.midY`)
- **Rotation**:
  - Pfeil rotiert mit `rotationEffect(.degrees((heading ?? 0) - mapHeading))`, damit der Pfeil immer in Bildschirmrichtung zeigt, auch wenn die Karte gedreht ist.

Referenz:

```35:50:/Users/bietiekay/code/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/common/UserHeadingAnnotationView.swift
private struct HeadingArrowShape: Shape {
    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let tipY: CGFloat = -11
        let baseY: CGFloat = 2
        let halfBase: CGFloat = 4.5

        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: tipY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: halfBase, y: baseY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: -halfBase, y: baseY))
        path.closeSubpath()

        let transform = CGAffineTransform(translationX: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
        return path.applying(transform)
    }
}
```

### 2) Heading-Aufbereitung (Kompass + Course + Glättung)

- `LocationManager` mischt **Course** (bei Bewegung) mit **Compass** (bei Stillstand).
- **Glättung** mit Exponential-Smoothing, inkl. Wrap-Around bei 0/360.
- `isHeadingValid` entscheidet, ob der Pfeil sichtbar ist.

Referenz:

```18:127:/Users/bietiekay/code/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/LocationManager.swift
@Published var userHeading: Double?
@Published private(set) var isHeadingValid: Bool = false
// ...
private func smoothHeading(_ newHeading: Double) -> Double {
    let normalized = normalizedHeading(newHeading)
    guard let last = lastSmoothedHeading else {
        lastSmoothedHeading = normalized
        return normalized
    }
    let delta = normalized - last
    let wrappedDelta: Double = {
        if delta > 180 { return delta - 360 }
        if delta < -180 { return delta + 360 }
        return delta
    }()
    let smoothed = normalizedHeading(last + wrappedDelta * headingSmoothingAlpha)
    lastSmoothedHeading = smoothed
    return smoothed
}
```

### 3) Kartenrotation & Kamera-Tracking

- `onMapCameraChange` liefert laufend `context.camera.heading` und Region.
- `currentHeadingDegrees` wird gespeichert und für Pfeil + Kompass verwendet.
- **Rotation aktiv** nur in Navigation (`settings.rotateMapDuringNavigation`).

Referenz:

```421:427:/Users/bietiekay/code/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/RootView.swift
.onMapCameraChange(frequency: .continuous) { context in
    let region = context.region
    currentRegion = region
    // Track current heading/rotation and full camera for resets
    currentHeadingDegrees = context.camera.heading
    currentCamera = context.camera
    // ...
}
```

### 4) Follow-Camera + Rotation während Navigation

- Zentral ist `updateFollowCamera(center:heading:)`.
- Bei Rotation wird `MapCamera(... heading: navHeading)` verwendet (iOS 17+).
- Kamera-Updates werden mit `.easeInOut(duration: 0.35)` animiert.

Referenz:

```904:943:/Users/bietiekay/code/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/RootView.swift
func updateFollowCamera(center coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D, heading: Double?) {
    // Skip updates during initial navigation zoom sequence
    guard !shouldPerformInitialNavigationZoom else { return }

    let shouldRotate = settings.rotateMapDuringNavigation && walkingRouteDestination != nil && heading != nil
    // ...
    withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.35)) {
        if shouldRotate, let navHeading = heading, #available(iOS 17.0, *) {
            let camera = MapCamera(
                centerCoordinate: coordinate,
                distance: targetRegion.span.latitudeDelta * 111000,
                heading: navHeading,
                pitch: 0
            )
            cameraPosition = .camera(camera)
        } else {
            cameraPosition = .region(targetRegion)
        }
    }
}
```

### 5) Urgent-Navigation: initiale Fit-Animation + verzögerter Zoom

- `applyRouteState` fitet zuerst Route+User+Ziel in die Region.
- Danach **verzögerter Zoom** (2.5s), um in den „Navigation-Look“ überzugehen.

Referenz:

```988:1047:/Users/bietiekay/code/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/RootView.swift
if fitCamera {
    // fit route + user + destination
    let fit = regionThatFits(coordinates: all, paddingFactor: 1.3)
    isProgrammaticCameraChange = true
    hasProgrammaticCameraSet = true
    withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.35)) {
        cameraPosition = .region(fit)
    }

    if isInitialRoute {
        shouldPerformInitialNavigationZoom = true
        Task {
            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 2_500_000_000) // 2.5 seconds
            await MainActor.run {
                if shouldPerformInitialNavigationZoom && walkingRouteDestination != nil {
                    performInitialNavigationZoom()
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### 6) Navigation-Overlay (NavigationOverlayKit)

- Overlay wird nur angezeigt, wenn `currentRoute != nil`.
- `NavigationOverlayViewModel` wird bei Route-Start befüllt und während der Fahrt aktualisiert.

Referenz:

```682:689:/Users/bietiekay/code/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/ToiletFinder/RootView.swift
if currentRoute != nil {
    NavigationOverlayView(viewModel: navigationOverlayViewModel, alignment: .topLeading, isWheelchairAccessible: settings.filterAccessibleToilets)
        .transition(.move(edge: .top).combined(with: .opacity))
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
}
```

public func update(with instruction: NavigationInstruction) {
    self.instruction = instruction
    self.remainingDistance = nil
}

public func updateRemainingDistance(to distance: Measurement<UnitLength>) {
    self.remainingDistance = distance
}
```

## Konkrete Umsetzungsschritte für die Ziel-App

1. **Map-Layer erfassen**: In der Ziel-App prüfen, ob SwiftUI `Map` mit `MapCameraPosition` genutzt wird. Falls `MKMapView` existiert, eine SwiftUI-Bridge oder entsprechendes Camera-API adaptieren.
2. **User-Annotation ersetzen**: Standard-User-Location ausblenden, Custom-Annotation mit `UserHeadingAnnotationView`-Pattern einbauen (Rotation = `heading - mapHeading`).
3. **Heading-Pipeline übernehmen**: Im Location-Manager die gleiche `blendedHeading` + `smoothHeading`-Logik aufbauen und `userHeading`, `isHeadingValid` publizieren.
4. **Map-Heading erfassen**: In `onMapCameraChange` `context.camera.heading` speichern; in einem `@State` halten.
5. **Follow-Camera-Logik**: `updateFollowCamera` wie oben implementieren, inkl. Rotation via `MapCamera(heading:)` bei Navigation.
6. **Urgent-Startsequenz**: Bei Route-Start (Urgent) `applyRouteState` mit initialem fit + Delay-Zoom ausführen.
7. **NavigationOverlayKit anbinden**: Route-Start → `NavigationInstruction` setzen; bei Location-Updates → `updateRemainingDistance` und `update(with:)`.
8. **Animationstiming übernehmen**: gleiche `easeInOut`-Dauern (0.35s) und Map-Transaction (0.45s) einbauen, damit die Bewegung gleich „smooth“ wirkt.

## Risiken/Abweichungen beim Port

- **MapKit API-Versionen**: `MapCamera` + Heading nur iOS 17+; für ältere Versionen Fallback über `region`.
- **Map-Update Loop**: `isProgrammaticCameraChange` verhindert unerwünschte Re-Searches; gleiche Schutzlogik in der Ziel-App nachbauen.
- **Heading-Quellen**: Bei niedriger Geschwindigkeit ist Compass-Heading dominant; in Fußgänger-Navigation ist das wichtig.

## Tests/Validierung (für den neuen Agenten)

- Check: Pfeil zeigt stets „screen-forward“ bei Kartendrehung.
- Check: Kompass erscheint >1° Drehung, Tap setzt auf North-up.
- Check: Urgent-Start: Fit → 2.5s → Zoom, danach flüssige Folgebewegung.
- Check: Overlay wird bei Route-Start aktiv und aktualisiert Distanz dynamisch.

        "contents": "---\nname: Navigation Overlay Mode\noverview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\ntodos:\n  - id: overlay-wireup\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into iPhone_DeviceNavigationView\n    status: completed\n  - id: sync-updates\n    content: Update overlay on route and location changes\n    status: completed\n  - id: docs-changelog\n    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n## Implementation plan\n\n### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view\n\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays.             "text": "    status: completed",
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "text": "  - id: docs-changelog",
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "text": "    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs",
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "    status: completed",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "isProject: false",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "## Implementation plan",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "text": "- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:",
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": "- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": "- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).",
            "lineNumber": 38
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.33458274602890015
    },

        "contents": "    private func calculateRoute(ignoreCache: Bool = false) {\n        // Calculate a new route between user and selected device.\n        // Prefers a cached route when movement &lt; 100m; applies a daily network request limit.\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        // Try to reuse cached route first unless explicitly told to ignore cache\n        if !ignoreCache {\n            if useCachedRouteIfValid() { return }\n            // Only recalc when one of the positions changed since the last route calculation (or if there's no route yet)\n            let userTimestampChanged = userTimestamp != lastRouteUserTimestamp\n            let deviceTimestampChanged = deviceTimestamp != lastRouteDeviceTimestamp\n            var userCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastUser = lastRouteUserCoordinate {\n                userCoordinatesChanged = (lastUser.latitude != user.latitude) || (lastUser.longitude != user.longitude)\n            }\n            var deviceCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastDevice = lastRouteDeviceCoordinate {\n                deviceCoordinatesChanged = (lastDevice.latitude != device.latitude) || (lastDevice.longitude != device.longitude)\n            }\n            let transportTypeChanged = settings.navigationTransportType != lastRouteTransportType\n            let shouldRecalculate = (route == nil) || userTimestampChanged || deviceTimestampChanged || userCoordinatesChanged || deviceCoordinatesChanged || transportTypeChanged\n            if !shouldRecalculate { return }\n        }\n\n        // Enforce daily limit through centralized counter with calendar-day reset\n        routeCounter.checkAndResetIfNeeded()\n        guard routeCounter.count &lt; routeRequestDailyLimit else {\n            showErrorOverlay(\n                \"Daily route request limit reached\",",

        "contents": "    private func openInAppleMaps() {\n        // Open the route in the Apple Maps app using the selected transport type\n        guard let dest = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        let source: MKMapItem\n        let destination: MKMapItem\n        if isRouteReversed {\n            source = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: dest))\n            source.name = device.DeviceName.isEmpty ? device.DeviceID : device.DeviceName\n            destination = MKMapItem.forCurrentLocation()\n        } else {\n            source = MKMapItem.forCurrentLocation()\n            destination = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: dest))\n            destination.name = device.DeviceName.isEmpty ? device.DeviceID : device.DeviceName\n        }\n        var options: [String: Any] = [:]\n        switch settings.navigationTransportType {\n        case 0: options[MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey] = MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeWalking\n        case 3: options[MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey] = MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeTransit\n        default: options[MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey] = MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeDriving\n        }\n        MKMapItem.openMaps(with: [source, destination], launchOptions: options)\n    }\n\n    private func transportTypeFromSetting(_ value: Int) -&gt; MKDirectionsTransportType {\n        switch value {\n        case 0: return .walking\n        case 3: return .transit\n        default: return .automobile\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func showErrorOverlay(_ debugMessage: String, _ userMessage: String) {\n        debugLog(\"Error: \\(debugMessage)\")\n        errorOverlayManager.show(message: userMessage, animationsAllowed: animationsAllowed)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Remote updates for the selected device only\n\n    private func fetchTargetDeviceLocation(resetAndRecenter: Bool, ignoreRouteCache: Bool = false) async {\n        // Fetch latest location for just the selected device from the server.",

Color.green : Color.primary)\n                .symbolEffect(.rotate.clockwise.byLayer, options: .nonRepeating, isActive: isUpdating)\n                .padding(.horizontal, 6)\n                .padding(.vertical, 8)\n                .contentShape(Rectangle())\n                .onTapGesture {\n                    if animationsAllowed {\n                        withAnimation { isUpdating = true }\n                    } else {\n                        isUpdating = true\n                    }\n                    Task {\n                        await fetchTargetDeviceLocation(resetAndRecenter: true, ignoreRouteCache: true)\n                        if animationsAllowed {\n                            withAnimation { isUpdating = false }\n                        } else {\n                            isUpdating = false\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                .onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.6) {\n                    // Toggle global setting for automatic route updates while navigating\n                    settings.automaticRouteUpdateDuringNavigation.toggle()\n                    isAutoRouteUpdateLocked = settings.automaticRouteUpdateDuringNavigation\n                    if settings.automaticRouteUpdateDuringNavigation {\n                        Haptic.notifySuccess()\n                        calculateRoute()\n                    } else {\n                        Haptic.notifyWarning()\n                    }\n                }\n                .accessibilityLabel(Text(NSLocalizedString(\"reload\", comment: \"Reload target device location\")))\n                .accessibilityHint(Text(NSLocalizedString(\"reload_longpress_hint\", comment: \"Long-press to toggle automatic route updates.\")))\n        }\n        .animation(animationsAllowed ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : nil, value: isAutoRouteUpdateLocked)\n        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)\n    }",

        "contents": "    private func refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() {\n        guard !isRouteReversed, let route else {\n            navigationOverlayViewModel = nil\n            lastOverlayStepIndex = nil\n            return\n        }\n        // Create and fully configure the view model before assigning so the view never shows\n        // the kit's default step (e.g. \"Arrive at destination\") for a frame when switching route\n        let newViewModel = NavigationOverlayViewModel(route: route, unit: navigationOverlayUnit())\n        let effectiveStepIndex: Int\n        if let location = locationManager.currentLocation,\n           let rawStepIndex = closestStepIndex(for: route, to: location.coordinate) {\n            // Never show \"Arrive at destination\" unless user is actually near the destination:\n            // if closest step is the last step, check distance to route end; if far, use step 0\n            let lastIndex = route.steps.count - 1\n            if rawStepIndex == lastIndex, lastIndex &gt; 0 {\n                let lastStep = route.steps[lastIndex]\n                let userPoint = MKMapPoint(location.coordinate)\n                let distanceToDestination = lastStep.polyline.closestDistance(to: userPoint) ?? auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).\n\n### 4) Documentation and changelog\n\n- Update &#96;[CHANGELOG.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/CHANGELOG.md)&#96; with the new “navigation instructions overlay in user→device mode”.\n- Update &#96;[APP_FEATURES.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/APP_FEATURES.md)&#96; (and/or &#96;[APP_STORE_DESCRIPTION.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/APP_STORE_DESCRIPTION.md)&#96; if you want it marketed) with a short note about in-app navigation instructions when routing from the current device to the selected device.\n\n### Key code touchpoints\n\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96;: add overlay view model, show overlay conditionally, update it when route changes, and update instruction step on location changes.\n  - Current route direction toggle and routing logic are already in place and will be reused:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n640:648:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift\n        if isRouteReversed {\n            request.source = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: device))\n            request.destination = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: user))\n        } else {\n            request.source = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: user))\n            request.destination = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: device))\n        }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The overlay should only show for “current device → other device” mode (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\n- NavigationOverlayKit is already added via SPM and available to the app target.\n\n## Testing\n\n- Manual test: start navigation to a device, switch direction to “current device → other device”, confirm overlay appears with instructions and updates as you move.\n- Verify: switch back to device→user hides overlay;     {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./APP_FEATURES.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {

          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 81
          }
        },
        "contents": "- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\n- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.\n- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).\n- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.\n- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\n- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&#96; draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. Auto‑centering gating is unified across views.\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; uses &#96;MKRoute&#96;, &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96;, and &#96;SettingsManager.navigationTransportType&#96; to render routes and progress; it recalculates on transport changes or movement thresholds and enforces a daily route‑request limit.\n- &#96;NavigationOverlayKit&#96; is used in &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; to show live turn‑by‑turn instructions when routing from the current device toward the target device.\n- &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96; estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; progress overlay rendering splits polylines into completed/remaining segments.\n- &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; is backed by &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96; for cached updates; &#96;MapCompass&#96; is shared.\n- &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96; groups arrow indicators by edge and scales coordinates; segments represent ~50 km and are capped at 10.\n- &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and label components use rasterized caching keyed by color/icon/height/colorScheme/scale and respect Dynamic Type and color scheme.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.",

        "contents": "    private func handleDeviceTap(deviceID: String, coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D) {\n        let tapStart = Date()\n        let nearby: [KnownDevice]\n        \n        if let precomputed = precomputedNearbyDevices[deviceID] {\n            nearby = precomputed\n            let elapsed = Date().timeIntervalSince(tapStart)\n            print(\"Device tap handled with precomputed nearby for \\(deviceID) in \\(String(format: \"%.3f\", elapsed))s (count: \\(precomputed.count))\")\n        } else {\n            nearby = nearbyDevices(around: deviceID, coordinate: coordinate)\n            let elapsed = Date().timeIntervalSince(tapStart)\n            print(\"Device tap computed nearby for \\(deviceID) in \\(String(format: \"%.3f\", elapsed))s (count: \\(nearby.count))\")\n        }\n        \n        if nearby.count &gt; 1 {\n            print(\"About to set devicePickerData with \\(nearby.count) devices: \\(nearby.map { $0.DeviceName })\")\n            devicePickerData = DevicePickerData(devices: nearby)\n            let elapsed = Date().timeIntervalSince(tapStart)\n            print(\"Device tap result for \\(deviceID): showing picker with \\(nearby.count) devices after \\(String(format: \"%.3f\", elapsed))s\")\n        } else if let first = nearby.first {\n            presentActions(for: first.DeviceID)\n            let elapsed = Date().timeIntervalSince(tapStart)\n            print(\"Device tap result for \\(deviceID): presenting actions for \\(first.DeviceID) after \\(String(format: \"%.3f\", elapsed))s (nearby count: \\(nearby.count))\")\n        } else {\n            presentActions(for: deviceID)\n            let elapsed = Date().timeIntervalSince(tapStart)\n            print(\"Device tap result for \\(deviceID): presenting fallback actions after \\(String(format: \"%.3f\", elapsed))s (no nearby devices)\")\n        }\n    }\n    \n    private func nearbyDevices(around deviceID: String, coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D, thresholdMeters: Double = 35) -&gt;         "contents": "---\nname: Improve Map Tapability\noverview: Add tap-friendly device action UI and overlapping-device picker on maps for iPhone/iPad.\ntodos:\n  - id: tap-hook\n    content: Add tap gesture to annotation hit area and show action sheet\n    status: completed\n  - id: overlap-picker\n    content: Detect nearby devices and show picker when overlapping\n    status: completed\n    dependencies:\n      - tap-hook\n  - id: hitbox-tuning\n    content: Enlarge/adjust transparent hitbox around markers\n    status: completed\n  - id: state-wiring\n    content: Add selection/action sheet state and reuse handlers\n    status: completed\n    dependencies:\n      - tap-hook\n  - id: a11y-polish\n    content: Add accessibility labels/hints for tappable areas and picker\n    status: completed\n    dependencies:\n      - tap-hook\n      - overlap-picker\n---\n\n# Make Device Map Annotations Tap-Friendly\n\n## Summary\n\nImplement tap-driven device action UI on map annotations, keep long-press context menus as fallback, and add a nearby-device picker when multiple markers overlap. Touch targets will be enlarged and consistent across iPhone/iPad map views.\n\n## Scope &amp; Files\n\n- iPhone device map: [&#96;miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceMapView.swift&#96;](miataru/views/iPhone/Devices%20Views/iPhone_DeviceMapView.swift)\n- iPad device map: [&#96;miataru/views/iPad/Devices Views/iPad_DeviceMapView.swift&#96;](miataru/views/iPad/Devices%20Views/iPad_DeviceMapView.swift)\n- (If shared helper needed) Common map helpers folder, or a small utility in the same files for distance-based grouping.\n\n## Plan\n\n1. Add tap entry point\n\n- On each device annotation wrapper, add &#96;.onTapGesture&#96; to the existing transparent hit area to open a new action surface (confirmationDialog or bottom sheet) mirroring current context menu actions (edit, navigation, history).\n- Keep &#96;.contextMenu&#96; for iPad/Mac as fallback/secondary.\n\n2. Resolve overlapping devices\n\n- Detect nearby annotations within a small distance threshold when a tap occurs (using coordinate distance on the map region). If more than one device is within threshold, present a selection sheet/list of device names to disambiguate; otherwise go straight to actions for the single device.\n\n3. Enlarge and align tap targets\n\n- Increase the transparent hit area around each marker (e.g., from 80x120 to ~120x160) and center it over the marker while preserving &#96;.contentShape(Rectangle())&#96; for reliable taps.",

0) - context.camera.heading) &gt; 0.1\n                if isProgrammaticCameraChange {\n                    // Ignore user interaction detection for programmatic updates\n                    isProgrammaticCameraChange = false\n                } else {\n                    if isFollowDeviceHeadingMode {\n                        followCameraDistanceOverride = context.camera.distance\n                        isFollowAutoZoomEnabled = false\n                    }\n                    // User interaction is detected via gestures; here we only deduce rotation state\n                    if abs(context.camera.heading) &lt; 0.1 {\n                        userHasRotatedMap = false\n                    } else if headingChanged {\n                        userHasRotatedMap = true\n                    }\n                }\n                currentMapCamera = context.camera\n                currentRegion = context.region\n            }\n            .overlay(alignment: .top) {\n                topOverlayStack\n            }\n            .overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing) {\n                scaleBarView()\n            }\n            .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) {\n                compassView()\n            }\n    }\n    \n    @ViewBuilder",

        "contents": "    }\n\n    class Coordinator: NSObject, MKMapViewDelegate {\n        var parent: iPad_LegacyMapViewRepresentable\n        \n        init(_ parent: iPad_LegacyMapViewRepresentable) {\n            self.parent = parent\n        }\n        \n        func mapView(_ mapView: MKMapView, rendererFor overlay: MKOverlay) -&gt; MKOverlayRenderer {\n            if let circle = overlay as? MKCircle {\n                let renderer = MKCircleRenderer(circle: circle)\n                let deviceColor = parent.device.DeviceColor ?? UIColor.blue\n                renderer.fillColor = deviceColor.withAlphaComponent(0.2)\n                renderer.strokeColor = deviceColor\n                renderer.lineWidth = 1\n                return renderer\n            }\n            return MKOverlayRenderer(overlay: overlay)\n        }\n        \n        func mapView(_ mapView: MKMapView, viewFor annotation: MKAnnotation) -&gt; MKAnnotationView? {\n            if annotation is MKUserLocation {\n                return nil\n            }\n            \n            let identifier = \"DeviceAnnotation\"\n            var annotationView = mapView.dequeueReusableAnnotationView(withIdentifier: identifier)\n            \n            if annotationView == nil {\n                annotationView = MKAnnotationView(annotation: annotation, reuseIdentifier: identifier)\n                annotationView?.canShowCallout = true\n            } else {\n                annotationView?.annotation = annotation\n            }\n            \n            // iPad-specific: Enhanced marker appearance\n            let deviceColor = parent.device.DeviceColor ?? UIColor.blue\n            annotationView?.image = createDeviceMarkerImage(color: deviceColor)\n            annotationView?.frame = CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 30, height: 30)\n            \n            return annotationView\n        }\n        \n        private func createDeviceMarkerImage(color: UIColor) -&gt; UIImage? {\n            let size = CGSize(width: 30, height: 30)",

MKMapView {\n        let mapView = MKMapView()\n        mapView.delegate = context.coordinator\n        mapView.isRotateEnabled = true\n        mapView.isPitchEnabled = true\n        mapView.showsUserLocation = false\n        mapView.setRegion(region, animated: false)\n        mapView.mapType = mapTypeFromSettings(mapType)\n        return mapView\n    }\n\n    func updateUIView(_ uiView: MKMapView, context: Context) {\n        uiView.setRegion(region, animated: true)\n        uiView.mapType = mapTypeFromSettings(mapType)\n        uiView.removeAnnotations(uiView.annotations)\n        if let coordinate = deviceLocation {\n            let annotation = MKPointAnnotation()\n            annotation.coordinate = coordinate\n            annotation.title = device.DeviceName\n            uiView.addAnnotation(annotation)\n            // Genauigkeitskreis\n            uiView.removeOverlays(uiView.overlays)\n            if settings.indicateAccuracyOnMap, let accuracy = deviceAccuracy, accuracy &gt; 0 {\n                let circle = MKCircle(center: coordinate, radius: accuracy)\n                uiView.addOverlay(circle)\n            }\n        } else {\n            uiView.removeOverlays(uiView.overlays)\n        }\n    }\n\n    func makeCoordinator() -&gt; Coordinator {\n        Coordinator(self)\n    }\n\n    class Coordinator: NSObject, MKMapViewDelegate {\n        var parent: iPhone_LegacyMapViewRepresentable",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * iPad_LegacyMapViewRepresentable.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\nimport UIKit\nimport MapKit\n\nstruct iPad_LegacyMapViewRepresentable: UIViewRepresentable {\n    @Binding var region: MKCoordinateRegion\n    let device: KnownDevice\n    let deviceLocation: CLLocationCoordinate2D?\n    let deviceAccuracy: Double?\n    let mapType: Int\n    @ObservedObject var settings: SettingsManager = SettingsManager.shared\n\n    func makeUIView(context: Context) -&gt; MKMapView {\n        let mapView = MKMapView()\n        mapView.delegate = context.coordinator\n        mapView.isRotateEnabled = true\n        mapView.isPitchEnabled = true\n        mapView.showsUserLocation = false\n        // iPad-specific: Force animations to be enabled\n        mapView.setRegion(region, animated: true)\n        mapView.mapType = mapTypeFromSettings(mapType)\n        return mapView\n    }\n\n    func updateUIView(_ uiView: MKMapView, context: Context) {\n        // iPad-specific: Always use animations for better user experience\n        uiView.setRegion(region, animated: true)\n        uiView.mapType = mapTypeFromSettings(mapType)\n        uiView.removeAnnotations(uiView.annotations)\n        if let coordinate = deviceLocation {\n            let annotation = MKPointAnnotation()\n            annotation.coordinate = coordinate\n            annotation.title = device.DeviceName\n            uiView.addAnnotation(annotation)\n            // Genauigkeitskreis\n            uiView.removeOverlays(uiView.overlays)\n            if settings.indicateAccuracyOnMap, let accuracy = deviceAccuracy, accuracy &gt; 0 {\n                let circle = MKCircle(center: coordinate, radius: accuracy)\n                uiView.addOverlay(circle)\n            }\n        } else {\n            uiView.removeOverlays(uiView.overlays)\n        }\n    }\n\n    func makeCoordinator() -&gt; Coordinator {\n        Coordinator(self)\n    }\n\n    class Coordinator: NSObject, MKMapViewDelegate {\n        var parent: iPad_LegacyMapViewRepresentable\n        ",
